subject: On‑site rack + nodegroup deployment checklist and next steps for Moontower
body:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Neal <liam.oneal@moontower.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: On‑site rack + nodegroup deployment checklist and next steps for Moontower

Hi Liam —

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. Attached is a concise checklist and an initial set of recommendations for the on‑prem Kubernetes deployment we discussed. High level asks we need from you to finalize the plan:

- Physical: rack IDs, PDU availability, top‑of‑rack switch models, expected cable pulls per rack.
- Network: uplink speed to aggregation (1/10/25/40/100Gb), VLAN numbering scheme, whether you use LACP for server uplinks, and whether BGP/EVPN is required between racks.
- Storage: primary shared storage (NetApp/Isilon/CEPH), export types (NFSv3/NFSv4/RBD/iSCSI), export paths, and whether you can expose block RBD.
- Security: on‑prem bastion jump host details, OOB KVM access, and IP allowlist for Redwood control plane.
- Workload profile: expected peak QPS for generation endpoints, median and 95th percentile sequence lengths, typical batch sizes, and model family (FP16/INT8) so we can size GPU memory.

Initial recommendations (summary) — full details in the attached PDF: redwood-onprem-checklist-v1.pdf
- Cluster topology: 3‑node control plane (HA), a small infra nodepool (monitoring/ingress), a realtime GPU nodepool (low‑latency A100/T4 depending on model), and a batch GPU nodepool for large jobs.
- Storage architecture: use your NetApp for persistent volumes (via NFS or iSCSI with external provisioner) for long‑term PK/metadata, and local NVMe for KV cache/ephemeral model caches.
- Node sizing (starting point):
  - control-plane: 3 x 8vCPU, 32GB RAM (no GPU)
  - infra: 2 x 8vCPU, 32GB RAM, 200GB SSD
  - realtime: 4 x A100 (40GB) nodes with 96vCPU, 768GB RAM (adjust for model)
  - batch: 2 x A100 (80GB) or equivalent for throughput jobs
- Network: recommend dedicating an L3 VLAN for model traffic, enable jumbo frames between nodes + storage, and ensure 10Gb+ for storage backplane.

Next steps: please attach the rack list and any facility FO/ODF plans; we'll produce a definitive nodepool and cabling diagram. Can we aim for a short call Thursday to lock the final IP subnets?

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Solutions
Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555‑0123

Attachment: redwood-onprem-checklist-v1.pdf (6 pages, checklist & nodepool templates)

From: Liam O'Neal <liam.oneal@moontower.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Moontower AI - Infra Ops <ops@moontower.ai>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 May 2028 10:04:22 -0700
Subject: Re: On‑site rack + nodegroup deployment checklist and next steps for Moontower

Marissa —

Appreciate the checklist. Some clarifications from our side:

- We have two production rooms (PRD‑A and PRD‑B) in the same campus. Each has N+1 PDUs and Mellanox/Arista top‑of‑rack with 25Gb uplinks to aggregation.
- Primary shared storage is NetApp ONTAP exposing NFS exports today; we can enable iSCSI/FC if needed, but NFSv4 is preferred by our storage team.
- GPU hardware at the moment is a mix: 4 x A100 40GB per rack + 2 x older V100 nodes in an adjacent cluster. We expect to refresh to 80GB GPUs in Q4.
- For security: we do not allow public IPs on the nodes; we have an on‑prem bastion with MFA we can provide access to.

Question: for KV cache and model MMAP performance, is it acceptable to rely on NetApp NFS for persistent volumes and then use local NVMe for hot caches? We want to avoid single‑point NFS spikes affecting inference latency.

Attached: site‑facility‑rack‑list.csv — contains rack IDs and U positions.

— Liam

Attachment: site-facility-rack-list.csv (CSV, 42 rows)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Neal <liam.oneal@moontower.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 May 2028 15:20:05 -0700
Subject: Re: On‑site rack + nodegroup deployment checklist and next steps for Moontower

Thanks — that matches our expectations and helps a lot. Short answers first, then an action plan below.

- KV cache: yes, use NetApp for persistent volumes (Prometheus, model checkpoints, long‑term storage) and put the KV cache and model shard caches on local NVMe. We recommend using a CSI driver to provision a local‑ssd StorageClass for caches (eviction on pod restart is OK).
- NFS single point: avoid exposing latency‑sensitive RPCs to NFS. For inference outputs/metrics it's fine, but the hot path (KV cache, embedding tables) should be local.

Proposed plan (deliverables we will produce):
1) Detailed nodepool mapping per rack — nodes labeled with rackID, U‑position, NIC mapping, NUMA zones.
2) Storage mapping — which NetApp export maps to which PVs, and RWO vs RWX choices per workload.
3) Network diagram — VLANs, BGP/EVPN requirements, MTU/Jumbo frame setting, and firewall rules for Redwood control plane.
4) Kube flags & tuning — kubelet, containerd, sysctl, NUMA affinity guide.
5) Rollout plan — canary traffic split, pod disruption budgets, and fallback to hosted model in case of capacity loss.

Preliminary nodepool sizes (we'll produce a spreadsheet):
- realtime‑tiny: 8vCPU, 64GB, 1 x A100 40GB (for prod low‑latency endpoints)
- realtime‑large: 96vCPU, 768GB, 4 x A100 40GB (for multi‑model pipelines)
- batch: 48vCPU, 384GB, 2 x A100 80GB (for offline async jobs)
- infra: 16vCPU/64GB (monitoring, logging, ingress)

Can we schedule a 30‑minute topology review Friday at 10:00 PT? If that works, we'll send an updated nodepool‑sizing table: nodepool-sizing-table.xlsx.

Best,
Marissa

Attachment: nodepool-sizing-table.xlsx (spreadsheet, 4 tabs)

Subject: Re: On‑site rack + nodegroup deployment checklist and next steps for Moontower

Quick tech notes from infra/serving runtime perspective — copying the action items into the runbook.

- OS/kernel: recommend Oracle/RedHat/CentOS 8+ kernel tuned for throughput: disable CPU C‑states, set irqbalance where appropriate, and enable transparent hugepages for certain model workloads.
- NUMA: pin GPU processes to NUMA zones that include the NVMe controllers. Avoid cross‑socket traffic for KV cache reads.
- I/O: use noop or none I/O scheduler for NVMe devices; ensure fio tests show <100µs tail latency for cache reads.
- Networking: enable GRO/LRO on the host for RDMA networks; if using Mellanox, use MLNX_OFED tuned with correct firmware.
- Container runtime: prefer containerd with CRI hook to pre‑warm model artifacts on startup. Kubelet flags: --eviction-hard=imagefs.available<10%,nodefs.available<5%, --kube-reserved=cpu=500m,memory=1Gi
- Storage plugin: if NetApp NFS is used, set mount options to nfsvers=4.1,rsize=1048576,wsize=1048576,hard,nointr and tune timeo/retrans for stable mounts.

I'll add these snippets to deployment-runbook-v0.9.pdf and include a short checklist for the onsite engineers to run during preflight.

— Dev

Liam / team —

Thanks for the confirmations and the rack list. Next operational steps from the Redwood side:

1) We will produce the final topology and cabling diagram by Wednesday and circulate for signoff.
2) Proposed maintenance window (non‑disruptive rehearsals) — weekend of Jun 17–18 for baseline installation, Jun 24 for canary traffic cutover.
3) SLA: Redwood will commit to 99.9% availability for the realtime endpoints post‑cutover with the following caveats documented in the runbook (storage misconfiguration, site power loss, or network fabric failure).
4) Contracting: please review the DocuSign for the Private Deployment Addendum; signing will allow us to ship the onboarding appliance and schedule an on‑site eng visit. DocuSign link: https://app.docusign.com/recipes/ABCD-2028-MOONTOWER

Action items for Moontower: share the facility rack elevations, confirm whether NetApp can expose iSCSI/RBD (helps with PV performance), and provide a temporary SSH jump host account for the Redwood field engineer.

If there's no outstanding technical blocker, Marissa and I will lock the call for Friday 10:00 PT and book the field eng for the week of Jun 14.

Thanks,

Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Customer Ops, Redwood Inference
stephanie@redwood.com | +1 (650) 555‑0199
